title: ALMA and VLA observations of the HD 141569 system
question: Is the shallow mm spectral index of the HD 141569 disc real, or is the 9 mm flux contaminated by stellar emission? What is the origin and variability of the 9 mm emission from HD 141569A, B and C?

data.bands: ALMA Band 3 (2.9 mm) archival; VLA Ka band (9 mm)
data.angular_resolution: ALMA 2.9 mm beam 0.69x0.52 arcsec, PA 56 deg

what.value: ALMA 870 um flux 3800±500 uJy, peak 1740 uJy/beam, beam 0.42x0.34
VLA 14A combined flux of B and C: 51±5 uJy

evidence.quote: we use $51 \pm 5~ \rm\mu Jy$ reported by (cite: macgregor)

evidence.loc: Millimetre Spectral Index of the Disc
evidence.quote: where $\beta_{s} = 1.8\pm0.2$ is a power law index for the dust opacity (cite: draine)

recipe.method: CLEAN with natural weighting to 0.5 sigma threshold

recipe.goal: Fit fluxes and positions in the uv plane
recipe.method: uvmodelfit point source for VLA; flat-intensity disc for ALMA
key_parameters: Uncertainties: sigma_rms plus 5% (VLA) or 10% (ALMA) calibration, in quadrature

recipe.goal: Derive mm spectral index and grain size slope q
recipe.method: Power-law fit F_nu ∝ nu^alpha between 870 um and 2.9 mm; q = (alpha_mm - alpha_pl)/beta_s + 3
Split data into ~5 min chunks, uvmodelfit each, compute brightness temperature from flux and stellar radius
assumptions: HD 141569A radius ~1.5 Rsun; M dwarf radius ~ R_Jupiter

evidence.quote: a $52\pm 5~\mu$Jy point source at the location of HD 141569A
The best fit flux is $149 \pm 9~ \rm\mu Jy$
We find a flux of $82 \pm 6~ \rm\mu Jy$ and $53\pm 5~\rm \mu Jy$ for VLA 14A and VLA 16A
we find a total flux of $420\pm 50~\mu$Jy

it would imply a brightness temperature of $\sim 5 \times 10^{6}$ K
we find brightness temperatures of $6\times10^{8}$ K and $< 2\times10^{7}$ K, respectively
